name: NY-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 11 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Tim Kennedy has a large financial advantage with $2.3M raised
Prediction markets price Kennedy near 96% to win
No public polling or expert ratings available for this race
model.rationale: The district's strong Democratic lean, Kennedy's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and markets pricing him near-certain all point to a comfortable win, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 21 points.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or an unexpected outside-spending surge for Hannon would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Kennedy, the Democratic incumbent, seeks reelection in a Buffalo-area district that voted about 11 points Democratic at the presidential level. He faces Republican Dennis Hannon, a challenger with no reported fundraising, while Kennedy has raised over $2.3 million and holds $1.2 million on hand. No public general-election polls or expert ratings exist for the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals and market pricing.

Prediction markets put Kennedy's chances near 96 percent, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating. The expected margin is roughly 21 points, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling. A major surprise in turnout or challenger resources would be needed to put the seat in play.
